items.summary: Researchers measured the polymorphic capacity of Claude Opus 4.6 acting as an automated malware generator using a dual-agent, four-stage pipeline to create a data-exfiltration payload. items.title: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning
items.one_liner: Sep-Latent uses separator tokens and attention decay to let LLMs perform efficient implicit reasoning with dynamic depth.
items.summary: While explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning enables LLMs to solve complex problems, its token verbosity introduces significant computational overhead. Although continuous latent space implicit reasoning offers an alternative, existing methods are constrained by fixed-length sequences and representational collapse. Researchers introduced Sep-Latent, an adaptive implicit reasoning framework that uses separator tokens as semantic anchors paired with an Attention-Decay mechanism to compress reasoning logic. Multi-level distillation aligns explicit and implicit layers, while dynamic query complexity controls latent thinking depth. On the GSM8k-Aug benchmark, Sep-Latent achieved 56.8% accuracy using an average of only 5.4 tokens, substantially improving efficiency over prior fixed-length models.
items.bottom_line: Separator tokens can serve as effective anchors for compressed latent reasoning in LLMs, closing the efficiency gap with explicit Chain-of-Thought.

items.title: An Agentic ENF Framework for Forensic Video Authentication Against Generative AI
items.one_liner: A new agentic forensic framework uses electric network frequency (ENF) consistency to reliably authenticate videos against generative AI manipulation.
items.summary: Because generative AI video models create realistic footage and traditional learned detectors degrade on unseen models, researchers developed an agentic forensic framework that authenticates videos using electric network frequency (ENF)—the power mains-driven hum in audio and flicker in video. A unified two-channel detector extracts ENF features, utilizing an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift model and synthetic injection training to overcome data scarcity, alongside a reference-matching channel to verify recording timestamps. A central finding is that generative videos contain ENF-band flicker indistinguishable from real footage, meaning authentication must rely on consistency against an independent reference rather than sheer presence. The detector successfully authenticates real audio and video at 93% and 100%, while an agentic orchestrator cuts execution time by 54% without losing accuracy.
items.bottom_line: Because generative AI videos replicate natural ENF flicker, video authentication must be based on time-reference consistency rather than raw signal presence.

items.title: Distill Until Divergence: Error-Truncated Hindsight Distillation for Agentic RL
items.one_liner: Error-truncated hindsight distillation routes positive and negative skills to prevent mismatched credit assignment in long-horizon agent RL.
items.summary: Long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning often relies on distilling completed trajectories into reusable skills to provide token-level credit, but skill-induced probability shifts can mismatch current states after an erroneous action occurs. To resolve this mismatch, researchers proposed a method that routes two complementary hindsight skills based on trajectory outcomes and error boundaries. Positive skills reinforce successful workflows and pre-error decisions, while negative skills target failure-specific corrections for decisive errors. Meanwhile, post-error suffixes are optimized exclusively via outcome-based GRPO without extending mismatched supervision. Experiments confirm that this approach improves fine-grained credit allocation and task performance.
items.bottom_line: Isolating post-error trajectory suffixes from mismatched skill supervision improves credit allocation in agentic reinforcement learning.

items.title: Reward Engine: Reward-Centric Self-Evolution for Open-Ended Tool Agents
items.one_liner: Reward Engine automatically builds frozen testcases and quality rubrics from initial trajectories to improve open-ended tool agent optimization.
items.summary: Researchers developed Reward Engine, a reward-centric self-evolution framework designed for open-ended tool agents operating in environments where executable ground-truth rewards are absent. The system works by analyzing tasks and initial trajectories to construct a static RewardPack comprising testcases for correctness and rubrics for graded quality, which then guides policy output selection and serves as a reward signal for reinforcement learning. Evaluations on WorkBuddy Bench Office and Claw-Eval show that the engine's constructed rewards largely agree with human benchmark graders without reversing their ordering on over 80% of candidate pairs. Additionally, using the engine to revise executions raised three-run consistency across baselines.
items.bottom_line: Self-generated, static testcase and rubric packs can effectively guide open-ended agent self-evolution without relying on explicit ground-truth functions.
